title: Key transit routes
steps: Barcelona airport → Andorra la Vella (arrival): Direct Bus runs seven scheduled departures a day per terminal (T1: 07:30, 11:00, 13:00, 15:00, 17:30, 20:00, 23:00; T2: +15 min each), ≈3h30 to the Estació Nacional d'Autobusos. {{fact:direct-bus-31-50-eur}} (confirm current fare at booking). Runs 365 days a year; 24/25/31 Dec and 1 Jan schedules may vary. Build in extra time at the airport end for EU biometric border checks (EES) on your first Schengen entry.

Andorra la Vella → Barcelona airport (departure): Same route in reverse, first departure 06:15, last 22:15. Book online and arrive 30 min early. For a same-day flight, leave enough buffer for the ≈3h30 ride plus airport time — the last bus that reliably makes an evening flight is well before the 22:15 final departure.

Getting around Andorra la Vella: the Barri Antic, Casa de la Vall, Sant Esteve and most hotels sit within a 10–15 minute walk of each other and of the bus station. Beyond that, the country runs seven regular national bus lines plus an Express and a Night bus. Two matter here: Line 1 (Escaldes-Engordany ↔ Sant Julià de Lòria), which runs through the capital and past Santa Coloma, and Line 2 (Andorra la Vella ↔ Encamp). ⚠ Timetables and fares live at bus.ad — check the day you travel.

To Llac d'Engolasters: the official signed route does not start at the lake — it starts in Encamp, in front of the Automobile Museum, reached on the Line 2 bus. From there it is 1.9 km out and back, rated Easy, +350 m/-45 m, about 1h15 up and 45 min down.

title: Weather
note: Early November in Andorra la Vella runs cold and damp — expect highs near 7°C, lows near -2°C, and a real chance of light snow at altitude. Pack layers and waterproof footwear.

title: Public holidays
note: Checked automatically against your travel dates. A national holiday can shorten hours or close shops, museums and the Casa de la Vall entirely — cross-check against the day plan before relying on a fixed opening time.
